items.content: Google launched Gemini 3.8 Flash, arriving just a few weeks after its predecessor. The company claims the new model “works harder” than Gemini 3.7 Flash by performing more reasoning steps on complex tasks and “calling tools iteratively.” It has the same introductory pricing as 3.7 Flash, $0.75 per million input tokens and $3.75 per million output tokens, but could still end up costing users more. Google warns that “the model might use more tokens to maximize performance, especially at higher effort levels.” Developers can keep using Gemini 3.7 Flash if they want to minimize token usage.Gemini 3.8 Flash’s launch was followed by some early impressions online. Artificial Analysis highlighted the model’s pricing, saying Gemini 3.8 Flash is “the cheapest we’ve measured at this level of intelligence. This is up ~40% from Gemini 3.7 Flash despite unchanged per-token pricing, driven by a 30% increase in output tokens per task and more turns on agentic evaluations.”Aigora.ai CEO John Ennis compared Gemini 3.8 Flash to Anthropic’s models, saying it offers “Opus 5 coding quality but at a fraction of the cost and super fast,” adding, “This is going to be so awesome for things like making remotion videos.”Google says Gemini 3.8 Flash offers “significant improvements” for software engineering and autonomous AI agents. It outperforms its predecessor and other frontier models on the DeepSWE v1.1 software engineering benchmark, including Anthropic’s Fable 5, which got an upgrade earlier this week that also promises stronger performance at a lower price, by cutting the price to use cached data.Google’s new model also outperformed its competitors on the Vals Finance Agent V2 benchmark and Harvey’s Legal Agent benchmark. However, the new model also “ships with safeguards against misuse in the domains of Chemical, Biological, Radiological, and Nuclear (CBRN) and cyber offense.”Google also released Gemini 3.8 Flash Cyber alongside its new Fairwind Program, which is limited to governments and “trusted partners.” The program, whose 650 members include CrowdStrike and the Center for Internet Security, offers access to 3.8 Flash Cyber and Google’s CodeMender agent, which Google says can help “autonomously find and fix vulnerabilities, protecting critical infrastructure, public services, and national security.” Gemini 3.8 Flash is available now for consumers with a Google AI Pro or Ultra subscription, as well as developers and enterprise users.

items.titleZh: 谷歌称其新的Gemini 3.8 Flash模型“工作更努力”，但成本可能更高
items.descriptionZh:
Google 在 Gemini 3.7 Flash 发布仅数周后便推出了新一代 Gemini 3.8 Flash。官方宣称，新模型在复杂任务中会执行更多推理步骤，并能够“迭代式地调用工具”，因此比前代“更努力地工作”。在定价上，Gemini 3.8 Flash 的入门价格与 3.7 Flash 保持一致：输入每百万 token 0.75 美元、输出每百万 token 3.75 美元，但由于新模型可能通过消耗更多 token 来追求更高性能，尤其是在高努力级别下，用户的实际成本可能上升。Google 也提示，希望严格控制 token 用量的开发者仍可继续使用 Gemini 3.7 Flash。

早期评测和用户反馈进一步揭示了其成本特性。Artificial Analysis 指出，Gemini 3.8 Flash 在同等智能水平下是“我们测过的最便宜的模型”，但单任务总成本依然比 3.7 Flash 高出约 40%，主要原因包括每个任务的输出 token 数量增加了 30%，以及在智能体评估中的交互轮次更多。Aigora.ai CEO John Ennis 将它与 Anthropic 的模型对比，认为其在编码任务上达到了“Opus 5 的质量”，但成本和速度优势明显，并特别提到它非常适合用于制作 remotion 视频等场景。

在技术性能方面，Google 表示 Gemini 3.8 Flash 在软件工程和自主 AI 智能体能力上实现了“显著提升”。它在 DeepSWE v1.1 软件工程基准测试中超越了前代及其他前沿模型，包括 Anthropic 本周早些时候刚刚升级的 Fable 5——该模型同样希望通过下调缓存数据的使用价格来提供更强劲且更经济的性能。此外，Gemini 3.8 Flash 还在 Vals Finance Agent V2 金融智能体基准和 Harvey 法律智能体基准上领先竞争对手。

为了防范滥用，新模型加入了针对化学、生物、放射性、核（CBRN）以及网络攻击等领域的保护措施。Google 还同步发布了面向政府和“受信伙伴”的 Gemini 3.8 Flash Cyber，以及名为 Fairwind 的专项计划。该计划目前拥有 650 个成员，包括 CrowdStrike 和互联网安全中心，参与者可以访问 Gemini 3.8 Flash Cyber 和 Google 的 CodeMender 智能体。后者能够“自主发现并修复漏洞，保护关键基础设施、公共服务和国家安全”。目前，Gemini 3.8 Flash 已面向 Google AI Pro/Ultra 订阅消费者、开发者及企业用户开放。

items.title: Microsoft will expand Windows 11 Memory Integrity feature to more PCs starting in October — security feature reduces gaming performance on some systems
items.description: Microsoft will begin enabling Memory Integrity by default on more eligible Windows PCs through quality updates in October, expanding kernel-level protection while preserving existing opt-outs for users who previously disabled the feature.
items.content: Copy link Facebook X Whatsapp Reddit Pinterest Flipboard Email Share this article 3 Join the conversation Follow us Add us as a preferred source on Google Newsletter Subscribe to our newsletter Microsoft will begin automatically enabling its Memory Integrity security feature on a broader range of eligible Windows PCs through quality updates starting in October 2026, extending the kernel-level protection to more existing devices by default. In a September 1 blog post, Microsoft said the rollout will provide stronger protection for more devices against attacks targeting the Windows kernel, while PCs that already have Memory Integrity deliberately disabled will retain their existing configuration.“Windows quality updates will begin enabling memory integrity protection on eligible devices,” Microsoft said. The updates will also enable Virtualization-based Security (VBS) where required, which provides the isolated environment underlying Memory Integrity. Before making the change, Windows will automatically assess each device using what Microsoft describes as readiness signals covering its hardware capabilities, compatibility, and performance.The October rollout is basically an expansion of Microsoft’s existing default-enablement policy. Memory Integrity is already switched on by default on clean Windows 11 installations that meet Microsoft’s hardware requirements, as well as on Secured-core PCs. Current requirements include an 8th Gen or newer Intel processor for Windows 11 22H2, an AMD Zen 2 or newer processor, at least 8GB of RAM on x64 systems, an SSD of at least 64GB, compatible drivers, and enabled hardware virtualization. Automatic activation under that policy applies to clean installations and not upgrades of existing devices.Latest Videos FromTom's HardwareWatch full video here: Memory Integrity — also known as Hypervisor-Protected Code Integrity (HVCI) — has existed since the Windows 10 era and was originally released as part of Microsoft’s Device Guard security technology. It uses VBS and the Windows hypervisor to move kernel-mode code-integrity checks into an isolated environment, helping prevent malicious or untrusted code and drivers from executing in the Windows kernel. Windows 10 generally left the protection optional outside configurations such as S mode, while Windows 11 made it more of a default security feature on compatible new installations.The feature comes with a performance wrinkle familiar to PC gamers, leading many gamers to disable it. Microsoft acknowledged in 2022 that Memory Integrity and Virtual Machine Platform could affect gaming performance on some Windows 11 configurations, and advised gamers prioritizing performance that they could temporarily disable these protections while playing, warning that doing so reduces security. The company’s own gaming guidance subsequently continued to recommend temporarily disabling Memory Integrity and VMP where they interfere with gaming performance. You may like Microsoft vows to make Windows 11 fly on 8GB RAM amid memory shortage Microsoft extends free Windows 10 security updates for a second year AMD will reinstate memory encryption on Ryzen 9000 CPUs through a BIOS update in July — TSME is coming back after 'valuable community feedback' The security feature’s impact on performance depends on the hardware. Microsoft says Memory Integrity performs better on newer processors with hardware features designed to accelerate the required isolation, while older CPUs relying on software emulation can experience a larger performance hit. Driver compatibility can also prevent activation, with Microsoft documenting issues ranging from malfunctioning software to incompatible gaming anti-cheat solutions.For most users, the October change requires no action. Eligible PCs will be evaluated and updated automatically, while administrator policies and previous user choices remain in place. Microsoft specifically says systems where Memory Integrity has already been disabled “won’t be automatically changed by this rollout,” leaving gamers and other users who previously opted out in control of the setting.Stay On the Cutting Edge: Get the Tom's Hardware NewsletterGet Tom's Hardware's best news and in-depth reviews, straight to your inbox.Contact me with news and offers from other Future brandsReceive email from us on behalf of our trusted partners or sponsors Follow Tom's Hardware on Google News, or add us as a preferred source, to get our latest news, analysis, & reviews in your feeds.

items.titleZh: 微软将自10月起将Windows 11的内存完整性功能扩展到更多PC——该安全功能会降低某些系统的游戏性能
items.descriptionZh:
微软昨日通过官方博客宣布了一项重要的安全更新计划：自2026年10月起，将通过Windows质量更新（Quality Updates）在更广泛的符合条件的PC上自动启用“内存完整性”（Memory Integrity）功能。这意味着这项针对Windows内核的防护措施，将从目前主要覆盖新装机的方式，扩展为面向更多存量设备默认开启。微软在9月1日的博文中明确表示，Windows质量更新将开始为符合条件的设备启用内存完整性保护，同时也会在需要的地方启用作为其底层支撑的基于虚拟化的安全（VBS）功能。在执行变更之前，Windows会根据硬件能力、兼容性和性能等多维度的“就绪信号”对每台设备进行自动评估。

此次2026年10月的推广，实质上是对微软现有默认启用策略的延伸。目前，在符合微软硬件要求的干净Windows 11安装以及安全核心PC（Secured-core PCs）上，内存完整性已被默认开启。以Windows 11 22H2为例，现有要求包括：第八代或更新的Intel处理器、AMD Zen 2或更新的处理器、x64系统至少8GB内存、至少64GB的SSD、兼容的驱动程序以及已启用的硬件虚拟化。值得注意的是，此前该策略下的自动激活仅适用于全新安装，而非对现有设备的升级，而到2026年10月后的这项新举措将使升级的已有设备也纳入默认启用的范围，但已有用户手动选择关闭的机器除外。

内存完整性，又被称为虚拟机监控程序保护的代码完整性（HVCI），最早可追溯至Windows 10时代，它最初作为微软Device Guard安全技术的一部分发布。其核心原理是利用VBS和Windows虚拟机监控程序（Hypervisor），将内核模式的代码完整性检查移入一个与操作系统隔离的安全环境中运行，从而有效阻止恶意或不受信任的代码与驱动程序在Windows内核中执行，从根本上保护系统核心免受攻击。在Windows 10时代，除了S模式等特定配置外，该保护普遍是可选项；而Windows 11则在兼容的新安装中将其定位为默认安全功能。

这项安全特性带来的性能损耗始终是PC玩家圈热议的话题，也是不少游戏玩家选择关闭它的原因。微软曾在2022年承认，内存完整性和虚拟机平台（Virtual Machine Platform）可能会对某些Windows 11配置下的游戏性能造成影响，并建议以性能为优先的用户可以在游戏时暂时关闭这些保护，但同时警告这会降低系统安全性。微软自家的游戏优化指南甚至也持续建议，在内存完整性和VMP干扰游戏性能时暂时将其禁用。需要指出的是，该功能对性能的实际影响高度依赖于硬件配置——微软称，在配备专门硬件加速隔离能力的新款处理器上，内存完整性表现相对更好；而依赖软件模拟的较老CPU则可能面临更明显的性能折损。此外，驱动程序兼容性也可能阻止该功能的启用，微软记录在案的问题既包括软件故障，也包括与某些游戏反作弊解决方案的不兼容。

对于大多数普通用户而言，2026年10月的这项变更无需任何手动操作：符合条件的PC将被自动评估并完成更新，而管理员策略和用户此前做出的选择也会得到尊重。微软特别强调，凡是已经手动关闭内存完整性的系统，都不会因这次推广而自动被重新打开。这意味着此前出于性能或其他原因选择关闭的玩家和用户，将保留对该设置的控制权，不会被强制变更。这项举措体现了微软在默认安全防护与用户自主选择之间寻求平衡的思路，未来几年，将推动更多存量Windows设备在无需用户干预的情况下具备抵御内核级攻击的底层能力。

items.title: GoPro to expand into AI data centers after $285 million merger with optical-photonics company — move to solve camera maker’s financial woes, move manufacturing back into the US
items.description: GoPro is merging with optical-photonics company Starman Optical in a deal worth at least $285 million. This move will wipe out the company's $92 million outstanding debt, let it start manufacturing its cameras in the U.S., and expand its portfolio to include optical transceivers for AI data centers.
items.content: Copy link Facebook X Whatsapp Reddit Pinterest Flipboard Email Share this article 0 Join the conversation Follow us Add us as a preferred source on Google Newsletter Subscribe to our newsletter GoPro just announced a merger with Starman Optical, Inc., an optical-photonics company, saying that the deal would allow the combined entity to produce U.S.-made optical transceivers for use in AI data centers. According to the press release, Starman will pay shareholders $285 million in cash for the action camera company, amounting to $1.14 per share, and will also pay off its outstanding debt of $92 million. Despite that, current GoPro investors will retain 10% ownership of the post-merger company.Go deeper with TH Premium: AI and data centers (Image credit: Microsoft)The data center cooling state of playThe custom AI ASIC state of play America’s AI chip rules keep changing — and the rest of the world is paying the priceGTC 2026: Ian Buck press Q&A transcript — VP of Hyperscale and HPC speaks out on shelving CPX and shipping LPU decode this yearDemand for data center CPUs has surged, and AI agents are responsibleStarman said that the move will give it access to GoPro’s intellectual property, which amounts to more than 2,500 patents, as well as its imaging solutions, advanced optics, and other technologies that it has developed. This deal is crucial in keeping the camera company afloat, especially as it has recently faced declining sales and increasing costs, leading the camera maker to warn investors that there is “substantial doubt about the company’s ability to continue.”On the other hand, the merger would expand GoPro’s portfolio to include optical transceivers, which are getting increased demand as AI data centers transition to fiber optics for their networking needs. Aside from data centers, the deal would also allow GoPro to expand into defense, government, robotics, and the aerospace industries, where it “intends to leverage its IP, optics, and imaging capabilities” to supply the increasing demand for solutions made within the U.S.Latest Videos FromTom's HardwareWatch full video here: While GoPro has successfully moved its manufacturing out of China to protect its supply chain from U.S. tariffs, it still has no local manufacturing. So, this merger would allow it to have production within American borders and help isolate it from further economic instability brought about by surprise tariff announcements.This could help it secure its future, especially as the FCC has recently been making moves to keep foreign-made tech like routers, LiDAR-equipped drones, and robots. It also makes sense for the two companies to partner — even though consumer action cameras and optical transceivers for data centers sound like they have nothing in common, they share a lot of technologies between them, like imaging sensors and advanced lenses or optics. You may like Elon Musk receives FTC greenlight to buy Mesh Optical as interconnects emerge as AI's tightest bottleneck AI data center optical interconnect market to hit $144 billion by 2030 Google signs $920M monthly compute deal with SpaceX This isn’t the first company with seemingly no relation to data centers to expand or pivot towards it. Struggling shoemaker and apparel brand Allbirds pivoted towards it earlier this year, resulting in a 580% jump in its stock price after the announcement, although it has since settled back down to its pre-announcement prices. AI data centers are indeed a tempting investment, with consultancy firm PricewaterhouseCoopers saying that investment on the technology could hit $32 trillion by 2050. items.titleZh: GoPro to expand into AI data centers after $285 million merger with optical-photonics company — move to solve camera maker’s financial woes, move manufacturing back into the US
items.descriptionZh:
GoPro宣布与光学光子学公司Starman Optical, Inc.达成合并协议，双方将组建一家新的实体，专注于生产美国本土制造的光学收发器，以满足AI数据中心不断增长的光纤网络需求。这一交易对于深陷财务困境的GoPro而言堪称关键转折，同时也标志着这家以运动相机闻名的消费电子企业在业务重心上的重大战略调整。

根据合并条款，Starman将以每股1.14美元、总计约2.85亿美元的现金支付给GoPro现有股东，并承担GoPro高达9200万美元的未偿债务。尽管如此，GoPro现有投资者仍将保留合并后新公司10%的股权。Starman方面表示，通过这笔交易，其将获得GoPro超过2500项专利的知识产权组合，以及公司在成像解决方案、先进光学系统和其他相关领域多年积累的技术资产。

这笔交易的背景是GoPro近年来所处的严峻经营形势。由于运动相机市场持续萎缩，销售额下滑而成本攀升，GoPro此前已向投资者发出警告，称公司持续经营能力存在“重大疑虑”。与Starman的合并显然为其提供了一条生存路径，使其能借助新实体的技术和市场方向彻底转型。

表面上看，运动相机与数据中心光学收发器似乎毫无关联，但两家公司指出了背后共享的核心技术：成像传感器、精密镜头与光学系统。正是这些底层能力，使GoPro现有的专利和研发积累能够平移到高速光通信领域。光学收发器是数据中心内部和之间用光纤传输数据的关键部件，随着AI大模型训练和推理对带宽需求激增，业界正加速从传统铜缆向光纤网络过渡，这让光学收发器成为供不应求的热门产品。

除数据中心外，合并后的公司还将依托GoPro原有的光学和成像能力，开拓国防、政府、机器人、航空航天等美国本土需求旺盛的领域。这一布局也与当前美国政策风向相吻合。值得一提的还有供应链安全考量。GoPro前些年为规避美国对华关税已将生产制造迁出中国，但它并没有自己的美国制造基地。此次合并后，新公司能够在美境内直接生产关键光学产品，进一步隔离突发性关税政策带来的经济不确定性。美国联邦通信委员会（FCC）近期也在收紧对路由器、搭载激光雷达的无人机、机器人等外国技术的准入限制，这使得“美国制造”的光学收发器更具战略价值。

市场对这类看似跨界转型的案例并不陌生。此前，经营不佳的鞋类及服饰品牌Allbirds也宣布向数据中心相关领域转型，消息公布后其股价一度暴涨580%，尽管后来回落至公告前水平。咨询公司普华永道预计，到2050年全球AI数据中心相关投资规模可能达到32万亿美元。显然，光学收发器作为AI基础设施的关键组件，已成为资本和产业竞逐的焦点。GoPro与Starman的合并能否复制甚至超越Allbirds的股价奇迹尚待观察，但至少，它为一家濒临破产的消费电子公司开出了一条通向AI时代核心赛道的新路。

items.title: Samsung teases new HBM5 with twice the performance of HBM4E —ambitious data transfer rates could hint at 4,096-bit interface
items.description: Samsung expects HBM5 to deliver 4 TB/s of bandwidth per stack by late 2020s, which will enable AI accelerators with aggregated memory bandwidth of around 100 TB/s.
items.content: Copy link Facebook X Whatsapp Reddit Pinterest Flipboard Email Share this article 4 Join the conversation Follow us Add us as a preferred source on Google Newsletter Subscribe to our newsletter The goal of next-generation HBM5 memory specification is to double performance and increase power efficiency compared to HBM4E, Samsung announced at the 'Memory Executive Summit,' an event that precedes 'Semicon Taiwan 2026.' Considering that it is barely realistic to double the data transfer rate of HBM4E in just one generation, the comment made by Samsung may imply that HBM5 will double the number of interface pins to boost bandwidth.Tom's Hardware Premium Roadmaps (Image credit: Future)Leading-edge foundry roadmapsNvidia Enterprise GPU and CPU roadmapAMD's Enterprise GPU and CPU roadmapIntel's roadmaps examined — 14A, Nova Lake, Diamond Rapids & AI accelerator pushCo-Packaged Optics (CPO) foundry roadmapsThe goal of HBM5, which is currently under development, is to double the performance and improve the performance per watt by 20% compared to the HBM4E generation, according to Choi Jang-seok, the head of the product planning team of the memory business department of Samsung Electronics DS division. Previously, Samsung announced that its HBM5 memory stacks will feature a heat path block (HPB), which will reduce thermal resistance by 20% and simplify cooling of HBM5 modules.Doubling HBM5’s per-stack memory bandwidth would result in peak bandwidth of around 4 TB/s per stack already in 2028 – 2029. TSMC expects AI accelerators to get to 20 – 24 HBM5/HBM5E per package configurations by the end of the decade, which means that these systems-in-packages will get a whopping 80 TB/s – 96 TB of memory bandwidth just several years down the road.Latest Videos FromTom's HardwareWatch full video here: Although both DRAM makers like Micron, Samsung, or SK hynix as well as developers of HBM controllers and PHYs like Cadence, Rambus, or Synopsys already offer HBM4/HBM4E controllers and interfaces rated for 16 GT/s data transfer rates, the official JEDEC transfer rate for HBM4E will be around 12 GT/s.If Samsung expects HBM5 to deliver twice the bandwidth of HBM4E, the HBM5 specification must either double the per-pin data transfer rate from 12 GT/s to 24 GT/s, double the interface width from 2,048 to 4,096 bits, or combine a wider interface with a higher data transfer rate. Increasing HBM5 memory stack interface width to 4,096 bits has so far been envisioned by KAIST and Marvell; however, this is certainly not an even semi-official confirmation of the specification's target. You may like Nvidia NVHBM promises 30% higher bandwidth, 15% lower power than commodity HBM4e JEDEC releases new SPHBM4 standard to slash AI memory costs Hot Chips 2026: SK hynix pushes hybrid bonding to HBM5 as AI memory hits 775-micron ceiling From a performance-per-watt perspective*, widening the interface is generally easier than doubling the per-pin signaling rate. Higher per-pin speeds require faster drivers, receivers, clocks, equalization, tighter timing margins, and a more sophisticated PHY since maintaining signaling integrity at speeds well beyond 20 GT/s is not easy. But while a wider HBM interface moves more bits in parallel at a lower speed per wire, going from 2,048 to 4,096 pins means twice as many TSV/I/O paths, drivers, receivers, bumps, more complicated routing, and extremely complicated base die. So while a 4,096 I/O at moderate speed is probably best for pJ/bit, the interface/package complexity gets so extreme that it may offset the gains. Furthermore, such a wide interface Perhaps a 3,072-bit interface combined with a moderate increase in data transfer rate would be a reasonable engineering compromise, though engineers involved in JEDEC’s decision-making process may think otherwise. In any case, for now, any discussion of HBM5 specifications remains speculative.Nonetheless, the target to double the bandwidth of HBM4E (2 TB/s per stack) within one generation is clearly a very aggressive one.Stay On the Cutting Edge: Get the Tom's Hardware NewsletterGet Tom's Hardware's best news and in-depth reviews, straight to your inbox.Contact me with news and offers from other Future brandsReceive email from us on behalf of our trusted partners or sponsors*It should be noted that achieving a 20% higher energy efficiency can be achieved not only by increasing performance, but by improving DRAM process technology, optimizing base die, lowering TSV I/O voltages, architectural changes, or power management. items.titleZh: 三星预告新HBM5，性能为HBM4E的两倍——数据传输速率雄心勃勃，或暗示4096位接口
items.descriptionZh:
三星电子在“Semicon Taiwan 2026”前的“存储器高管峰会”（Memory Executive Summit）上透露，正在开发的下一代HBM5内存规格目标是将每堆栈性能相比HBM4E翻倍，同时将每瓦性能（能效）提升20%。这一目标由三星电子DS部门存储器业务产品规划团队负责人崔章锡（Choi Jang-seok）宣布。考虑到在一代产品内实现数据传输率翻倍几乎不现实，这一表态很可能意味着HBM5将大幅增加接口引脚数量，以并行度换取带宽。

三星此前已宣布，其HBM5堆栈会引入“热路径块”（Heat Path Block, HPB）设计，可将热阻降低20%，从而简化HBM5模块的散热方案，为更高功耗和更紧凑的封装创造条件。如果HBM5的每堆栈带宽确实比HBM4E翻倍，那么到2028至2029年，单个HBM5堆栈的峰值带宽将达到约4 TB/s。台积电预计，到本十年末，AI加速器单个封装将配置20至24个HBM5/HBM5E堆栈，这意味着系统级封装的总内存带宽将达到惊人的80 TB/s至96 TB/s，为超大规模AI训练和推理提供前所未有的数据吞吐能力。

从技术路径来说，目前三星、美光、SK海力士等DRAM厂商，以及Cadence、Rambus、Synopsys等HBM控制器和物理层（PHY）开发商，已经提供支持16 GT/s数据传输率的HBM4/HBM4E控制与接口方案，但JEDEC官方规范中HBM4E的数据速率约为12 GT/s。若HBM5要达到两倍于HBM4E的带宽，规格设计上必须做出选择：要么将每引脚速率从12 GT/s翻倍至24 GT/s；要么将接口宽度从目前的2048位扩展至4096位；或者同时扩大接口宽度并适度提高速率。目前韩国科学技术院（KAIST）和Marvell已提出4096位接口的设想，但这并非JEDEC的官方确认，HBM5规格至今仍属推测阶段。

从单位能耗传输效率（pJ/bit）来看，扩宽接口通常比提高每引脚速率更有利。超过20 GT/s的信号速率需要更快的驱动器、接收器、时钟与均衡电路，时序裕量更紧张，PHY复杂度显著增加，维持信号完整性极富挑战。但若将接口宽度从2048位增加至4096位，也意味着两倍的硅通孔（TSV）和I/O路径、驱动器、接收器、微凸点，以及极其复杂的基片（base die）布线和封装路由，这种极端接口复杂度可能抵消能效收益。因此，业内认为采用3072位接口配合中等速率提升，或许是一个合理的工程折中方案，但JEDEC的决策工程师可能另有权衡。

值得注意的是，实现20%的能效提升并非只能依靠带宽增加。改进DRAM工艺技术、优化基片设计、降低TSV I/O工作电压、改善架构或引入更精细的功耗管理，同样能达成目标。HBM5在单个世代内将HBM4E（每堆栈约2 TB/s）带宽翻倍，确实是一个非常激进的目标，其最终规格如何平衡速率、接口宽度、功耗与封装复杂度，将对未来AI芯片设计产生深远影响。

items.content: New York City mayor Zohran Mamdani has announced a new policy today that will ban younger schoolchildren from using AI in classrooms. The one-year moratorium, effective in the 2026-2027 school year, will impact about 600,000 public school students in 2-K through eighth grade and is being introduced alongside additional limits on digital devices and a small pilot program for AI education tools.The new rules being introduced by NYC’s Department of Education will bar teachers from using AI tools to grade assignments, and keep students from using the technology in the classroom until they enter high school, with chatbots designed specifically for companionship and mental support reportedly being banned in all grades. High school aged students will only be permitted to use AI in specific instances, and they’ll be offered AI literacy classes twice a year to help students “think critically” before they come to “rely on it.”“Children need teachers and human connection in order to learn and grow. They need to develop skills alongside their peers, build relationships with educators, and wrestle with tough problems on their own,” Mamdani said in a statement. “The tech industry wants us to believe that AI-powered early education is not only inevitable, but necessary. We do not see it that way.”RelatedSome of the nation’s rich are letting AI teach their kidsThe problems with AI in schoolsThe more young people use AI, the more they hate itUse of individual screens will be banned until third grade. The department is also issuing recommended screen time limitations, which include a maximum of 45 minutes per day for middle schoolers. Teachers will still be permitted to use AI for lesson planning, and exceptions may be granted for AI tools that help students with disabilities or multilingual students. Exceptions can also be granted for particular purposes like computer science programs.A “limited AI pilot” program will also be offered at up to five classes in a “small number” of high school classrooms, using tools that were vetted to meet safety and data privacy standards, and “keeping students as the primary thinker.” Tools being piloted by this program have set time limits for usage, and include Quill for English language support, Edia for math, Brisk Teaching for guiding study practice, and Playlab and Intel AI-Ready Schools for multi-subject support.These changes follow NYC’s public school system introducing a bell-to-bell ban on “personal internet-enabled electronic devices” (including smartphones) for the 2025-2026 school year. NYC district leaders say the new AI moratorium for classrooms is one of the most restrictive policies in the US, though some countries like Norway, Sweden, and the Netherlands have implemented nationwide changes to address similar concerns about the impact that technology is having on developing minds.

items.titleZh: NYC bans AI use for students until they reach high school
items.descriptionZh:
纽约市市长佐赫兰·马姆达尼于今日宣布一项重磅教育新政：全市公立学校将禁止低年级学生在课堂上使用人工智能工具。这项为期一年的暂停令将从2026-2027学年起生效，覆盖从学前班（2-K）到八年级的约60万名学生，同时配套出台数字设备使用限制，并启动一个小规模AI教育工具试点项目。

新规由纽约市教育局制定，核心内容包括：禁止教师使用AI工具批改作业；学生在进入高中之前不得在课堂上使用AI技术；面向全年级的“AI陪伴”或“AI心理支持”类聊天机器人被完全禁止。高中生仅可在特定场景下使用AI，且每年需参加两次AI素养课程，其目的在于帮助学生在“依赖AI之前”学会“批判性思考”。

马姆达尼在声明中强调：“孩子的学习和成长需要教师和真实的人际连接。他们需要与同龄人一起培养技能、与教育者建立关系，并独立面对难题。科技行业试图让我们相信AI驱动的早期教育既不可避免又不可或缺，但我们不这样认为。”

在具体措施上，纽约市教育局还规定：三年级以下学生全面禁用个人电子屏幕；初中生每日屏幕时间上限为45分钟。不过，教师仍可使用AI辅助备课；帮助残障学生或多语言学生的AI工具可以申请豁免；计算机科学等特定教学项目也可获得豁免。

与此同时，教育局将推出一个“有限AI试点”项目，在少数高中班级中最多五个课堂使用经过筛选的AI工具。这些工具必须满足安全和数据隐私标准，并确保“学生始终是主要思考者”。试点工具设有明确使用时间限制，包括：支持英语学习的Quill、数学辅导Edia、学习指导Brisk Teaching，以及支持多学科教学Playlab与Intel AI-Ready Schools。

这项政策与纽约市公立学校此前推行的“铃间禁令”一脉相承——2025-2026学年起，学生全天禁止携带智能手机等个人联网电子设备。纽约学区负责人表示，这一新的AI课堂暂停令是全美最严格的同类政策之一。不过，挪威、瑞典、荷兰等国已采取全国性措施，应对科技对青少年心智发展的潜在影响，纽约并非孤例。

items.title: FBI investigating 153 million US and Canadian driver’s licenses leaked on Russian cybercrime forum, including that of US SecDef Pete Hegseth — data is suspected to have come from an ID-authentication service provider
items.description: The leak was traced to a major ID-authentication service based in Louisiana, serving major companies like Hertz, Target, and the United States Coast Guard.
items.content: Copy link Facebook X Whatsapp Reddit Pinterest Flipboard Email Share this article 1 Join the conversation Follow us Add us as a preferred source on Google Newsletter Subscribe to our newsletter More than 153 million US and Canadian driver’s licenses, as well as other identity documents, have reportedly become available for purchase on the dark web for a limited time. According to cybersecurity journalist Brian Krebs, the service was called Nexus, and although it’s no longer available at the time of writing, it claimed to have possessed 153 million driver’s licenses, 10 million ID cards, 1.9 million travel documents, 1.3 million international driver’s licenses, 579k medical cards, 429k common access cards, 91k residence cards, 77k employment authorization records, and 5 million other documents, allegedly sourced from an ID-authentication service based in Louisiana.The service was advertised on the Russian cybercrime forum Exploit, where whoever was promoting it posted the driver’s license of Krebs as a free sample, which caught the journalist’s attention. He was also able to see a preview of U.S. Secretary of Defense Pete Hegseth’s information on the database — a concerning breach of security for someone with such a sensitive position in the government. After further investigation, they concluded that the service seemed to have possessed legitimate data, especially after searching for the data of several of his friends and family members with their consent. One thing that all the people he found in the database had in common was that they all used Hertz to rent a vehicle.Krebs also talked with security and privacy researcher Zach Edwards, who said that their information was also found on Nexus. Edwards said that they did not rent a car recently but used their ID at a Planet13 marijuana dispensary. The time stamps found on the scanned images of the driver’s licenses and other identity documents coincide with the time that the victims used their IDs at the said companies, confirming that they were the sources of the leaks. However, Planet13 and Hertz do not do their own authentication; instead, they contract a service provider for the service. Now, it turns out that both Planet13 and Hertz used the company for identity verification and ID-authentication — IDScan.Latest Videos FromTom's HardwareWatch full video here: Based on the evidence gathered by Krebs, it seems that the leak is centered around the company. He has already contacted the company about the issue, and they said they were investigating the matter. “At this point I’m not able to share any additional information, but the updates you have provided have been welcome, and helpful to our team’s investigation,” Jillian Kossman, a marketing and operations leader at idscan.net, told the journalist. The FBI has also started looking into the leak, with its New Orleans field office opening an official investigation into the breach.The massive amount of data that was briefly available on the dark web is certainly concerning. A similar data breach hit Discord after its third-party service provider was hit and resulted in the exposure of 70,000 government IDs. Incidents like these have got privacy experts concerned with the push for online age verification requirements, which is why the EFF is asking the California governor to veto the law requiring this. Driver’s licenses are often widely accepted for opening credit lines and bank accounts, with both photographic, UV, and IR scans available on many of the leaked licenses. Aside from that, it could also potentially compromise the privacy and security of vulnerable people, like those fleeing domestic violence and those who are under the witness protection program. items.titleZh: FBI investigating 153 million US and Canadian driver’s licenses leaked on Russian cybercrime forum, including that of US SecDef Pete Hegseth — data is suspected to have come from an ID-authentication service provider
items.descriptionZh:
据网络安全记者Brian Krebs报道，一个名为Nexus的暗网服务在短暂运营期间，公然出售超过1.53亿份美国和加拿大驾照及其他身份证明文件。虽然该服务在本文撰写时已无法访问，但其宣称掌握的数据规模令人震惊：包括1.53亿份驾照、1000万张身份证、190万份旅行证件、130万份国际驾照、57.9万张医疗卡、42.9万张通用访问卡（CAC，常用于军事设施）、9.1万张居留卡、7.7万份就业授权文件，以及500万份其他类型证件。据称这些数据源自路易斯安那州一家身份验证服务公司。

该服务在俄罗斯网络犯罪论坛Exploit上打广告，发帖者甚至免费提供了Krebs本人的驾照作为“样品”，这引起了这位记者的注意。他还在数据库中预览到了美国国防部长皮特·赫格塞斯的信息——对于如此敏感职位的政府官员而言，这是令人担忧的安全漏洞。经过进一步调查，Krebs认为该服务确实掌握了真实数据，尤其是在征得朋友和家人同意后，他搜索到了他们的信息。所有被查到的人员有一个共同点：他们都使用过Hertz租车服务。

Krebs还与安全和隐私研究员扎克·爱德华兹进行了交流，后者表示自己的信息也出现在Nexus上。爱德华兹提到，他近期并未租车，而是在一家名为Planet13的大麻药房使用过身份证件。数据库扫描图像上的时间戳与受害者在这些商家使用身份证件的时间吻合，从而确认了数据来源。然而，Hertz和Planet13并不自行执行身份验证，而是将这项业务外包给第三方服务商。调查表明，两家公司都使用了同一家身份验证和ID认证公司——IDScan.net。

基于Krebs收集的证据，此次泄露的核心指向该公司。Krebs已与IDScan.net联系，对方回应正在调查此事。该公司的市场和运营负责人Jillian Kossman表示：“目前我无法分享更多信息，但您提供的线索对我们团队的调查非常有帮助。”美国联邦调查局（FBI）也已介入，其新奥尔良外勤办事处已对这起泄露事件正式立案调查。

这类大规模数据泄露并非孤例。此前，Discord因第三方服务商遭受攻击，曾导致7万份政府身份证件泄露。此类事件引起隐私专家的高度警惕，尤其是当前各界正推动在线年龄验证立法——电子前沿基金会（EFF）因此呼吁加州州长否决相关法案。除了侵犯隐私、践踏第一修正案权利之外，敏感数据的泄露还可能加剧身份盗窃案件。驾照通常被广泛接受为开设信贷额度和银行账户的凭证，而此次泄露的许多驾照扫描件同时包含照片、紫外线和红外线扫描数据。更严重的是，这可能危及弱势人群的隐私和安全，例如逃离家庭暴力的受害者以及受证人保护计划保护的人员。

items.title: Fractal Define One case review: Balancing noise and thermals
items.description: Fractal’s Define One rounds off the boxy Define, while still keeping the iconic closed-front design. A focus on GPU airflow and three included Momentum 14 fans highlight this $154 mid-tower chassis.
items.content: The Fractal Define series has been around since 2009, starting with the aptly named Fractal Define chassis. Since then, we’ve seen the Define R2/R3/R4/R5/R6/R7/7 XL cases over the years, all keeping the familiar closed-front design. Today, Fractal released the Define One, which they say is a “...modern expression of quiet performance and Scandinavian aesthetics”. This ‘expression’ includes aluminum side intake vents, premium details, and subtle curves that aim for a clean, understated look balancing airflow and thermal efficiency.The new Define One achieves Fractal’s goals, offering users a clean, premium-looking chassis that achieves sound mitigation with its closed-front design. The previous Define 7 and 7 XL (and others before it) are all cuboids with sharp edges, whereas the Define One rounds the corners off for a softer, yet still premium appearance. This is one of the best-looking Define chassis to date.Inside, there’s room for large graphics cards, multiple radiators (up to 360mm), and it even supports rear-connect motherboards. Fractal includes three pre-installed Momentum 14 fans in the front and has a unique integrated front air guide that feeds air directly from the bottom fan towards the video card. The interior is well thought out, with toolless access, removable brackets, and built-in cable management that makes building easier and leaves you with a clean, functional PC. Priced at $154.99, it gives off premium vibes you don’t normally find at this price point, or in previous Define iterations.We'll cover many more details inside and outside the chassis, showcasing the features and any issues we may encounter during the build process. We also run the case through thermal and noise testing to show how it performs compared to others and whether it has a chance of making our best PC cases list. Below are the case's specifications from Fractal.Latest Videos FromTom's HardwareWatch full video here: Define One Product Specifications Swipe to scroll horizontally Type Mid-Tower Dimensions (H x L x W) 19.6 x 18.9 x 9.2-inches (500 x 482 x 235mm) Motherboard Support Mini-ITX, Micro ATX, ATX, E-ATX Back-connect Motherboard Support No Color Dark Solid Dark TG Light TintLight SolidLight TG Clear Tint Storage Support (2) 3.5-inch -or- (4) 2.5-inch(Supports up to six 2.5-inch total) PCIe Expansion Slots 7 Fan Support Top - 2x120/140mmFront - 3x120/140mmBottom - N/ARear - 1x120mm Pre-installed fans (3) 140mm LCP Blade Momentum 14 (Front) Radiator Support Front - Up to 360mmTop - Up to 280mmRear - 1x120mm CPU Cooler Clearance 171mm GPU Clearance 368mm (w/ front fans installed)338mm (w/ 30 thick front rad. installed) Vertical GPU Support Yes (required adapter, $79.99) PSU Length 180mm Dust Filters Top, Front, Bottom Other features 3x included fans, integrated GPU front air guide, noise/vibration dampening MSRP $154.99 (all four configurations) Warranty 2 Years Today's best Fractal Design Define One deals No price informationCheck AmazonWe check over 250 million products every day for the best pricesFeatures of the Define One▶️ External FeaturesExternally, the case looks considerably different than previous versions. While it still screams "computer case," those rounded edges soften the look of the closed-front design. The IO panel is still on top, and there’s a single LED at the top of the front panel, like previous designs. Another holdover is the ability to take the chassis apart for easy access, a boon for building. Overall, I do like the look of the 'Light' colorway. The subtle rounding off of sharp edges makes the Define One stand out among past iterations. It comes in four flavors: Dark (black) and Light (off-white) with closed sides, or Dark with tinted tempered glass and Light with tempered glass and no tint – one should match your style and build preferences. Image 1 of 7 (Image credit: Future) (Image credit: Future) (Image credit: Future) (Image credit: Future) (Image credit: Future) (Image credit: Future) (Image credit: Future) Image 1 of 7 View Original Image 2 of 7 View Original Image 3 of 7 View Original Image 4 of 7 View Original Image 5 of 7 View Original Image 6 of 7 View Original Image 7 of 7 View Original The side of the off-white Light case uses a clear tempered glass panel, secured by three tabs at the bottom and held to the frame by two ball-and-socket latching mechanisms on top. Slot the glass in and push on top and you're done. The clear glass allows for unobstructed views of the internals and easy access to the components inside. The other side panel is solid and bitumen-lined for sound dampening (like the front panel), and it attaches the same way, with tabs at the bottom and ball-and-socket mechanisms on top. Both have a small indentation at the top and rear of the case where you can easily grab and remove the panels.Intake also comes through the sides. Two aluminum strips run vertically with small circular perforations, and on the Light chassis, the strips contrast with the rest of the off-white case and look good, breaking up the otherwise all-white colorway. These intakes also use a removable dust filter, accessible from the inside when you take off the front panel. It’s not the best situation for high airflow, but as we’ll see later, the Define One didn’t do a terrible job in our testing, especially on the GPU, using only one additional case fan, leaving the top empty.Turning the chassis around to the rear, we get a better view of the seven expansion slots (which also have a cover over the screws to clean up the appearance), the rear fan location supporting 120mm air movers, and the PSU mounting location at the bottom. The power supply uses a bracket with two captive thumbscrews. Simply mount it to your power supply, then install it in the case. Looking on the left, you’ll also see a couple of pre-installed Velcro straps to help with internal wire management.Stay On the Cutting Edge: Get the Tom's Hardware NewsletterGet Tom's Hardware's best news and in-depth reviews, straight to your inbox.Contact me with news and offers from other Future brandsReceive email from us on behalf of our trusted partners or sponsorsThe bottom of the Define One uses a raised gray plastic frame that circles the entire bottom, with rubber ‘feet’ on the corners, giving your power supply about an inch of room to breathe. The dust filter on the bottom pulls out from the left side (window side), which is ideal since you likely won’t have to move your PC to remove it. In many cases, it comes out from the rear, requiring you to move your heavy PC to clean it. Image 1 of 2 (Image credit: Future) (Image credit: Future) Image 1 of 2 View Original Image 2 of 2 View Original On top of the case, Fractal updated the design with a dense pattern of circular holes for air to pass through. This feels a bit more restrictive than the more open design on the Define 7, but still allowed air to escape even without fans on top in our testing. The good news, at least when this area is used as exhaust, is that there isn’t a mesh dust filter to thwart airflow further. The top panel also pops off easily (via more ball-and-socket retention clips) from the back, exposing the inner frame where you mount fans or a radiator.The IO panel sits at the front edge and offers your typical assortment of ports. You get three USB ports: one USB 3.2 Gen 2x2 20 Gbps Type-C, and two USB 3.1 Gen 1 (5 Gbps) Type-A ports. This is exactly what we want to see in a case of this caliber. There’s also a shiny power button with the Fractal symbol in the middle, a 3.5mm combo audio jack on the left, and finally a skinny LED light at the top. The front panel also comes off easily. Removing the top panel exposes two levers, so you can remove the front panel, access the front of the case, and reach those three 140mm Momentum 14 fans and dust filters.▶️ Internal FeaturesInside the case, you have two separate chambers. One is for the power supply and cables, while the other is for the components. One of the first things that jumped out to me is the integrated front air guide, which helps direct airflow to the graphics card. I like this, as the front bottom fans' air isn’t wasted on the power supply and instead focuses on what is likely the hottest-running component. Just above that is the adjustable support bracket for the video card, mounted directly to the motherboard tray. Two screws let it move a couple of inches up or down, so it supports video cards of nearly any size.Next up is the motherboard tray, and it has plenty of cutouts. The largest one, behind the socket, is great for accessing the rear of the motherboard and mounting your cooling solution while the board is in the case. The rest are there for cable management (top or bottom) and to support rear-connect motherboards like Asus BTF, Gigabyte Stealth, and MSI Project Zero boards. A large gray grommet for hiding wires runs vertically to the right of the motherboard. This grommet satisfied a pet peeve of mine by not moving out of its spot easily, as some others do. In fact, in some cases I’ve owned, I’ve glued the grommets in because I was tired of them pulling out when building or changing parts. You can mount a 3x120 mm radiator here, with a maximum length of 405 mm and 30 mm thick if you keep the air guide (435 mm and thicker radiators, up to 65 mm, if you remove it), or it fits 280/240/140/120mm radiators. There are plenty of options, but make sure you know your radiator size so you know what you need to remove, if anything.Looking at the ceiling of the case from the inside, we see the removable top bracket, held in by two screws. The top holds up to two 140mm fans or a 280mm radiator. You have around 60mm or so before the radiator/fan combo covers the top of the motherboard, so you don’t have to worry too much about fitment or covering the top of your motherboard if you choose to use a radiator in this space. At the rear of the case, we spy the 120mm fan mounting location and the seven available expansion slots.On the bottom rear, we can see the power supply chamber, along with space to route cables for any headers located along the bottom of the motherboard. On the left are two plastic pieces and pre-installed Velcro. The plastic pieces slide in and out so you can more easily get the cables in the channel.On the rear of the case are more Velcro straps to route cables, like your 8-pin EPS for the CPU, cleanly up the back. items.titleZh: Fractal Define One 机箱评测：平衡噪音与
items.descriptionZh:
Fractal Design（分形工艺）的Define系列机箱自2009年首款Define问世以来，历经R2至R7、7 XL等多代迭代，始终遵循标志性的封闭前面板设计，主打静音与北欧极简美学。如今，该系列迎来了全新成员——Define One，官方将其定义为“静音性能与斯堪的纳维亚审美的现代演绎”。这款中塔机箱在保留封闭前脸降噪理念的同时，引入了更具亲和力的圆润边角、铝制侧进气格栅和高级质感细节，在空气流通与散热效率之间寻求平衡，成为Define家族中外观最为柔和且精致的一款。

外观设计上，Define One提供了四种配色方案：暗黑（纯黑）与浅白（米白）可选全封闭钢板侧板或透明钢化玻璃侧板，玻璃版本还分浅色透明与无着色两种。评测的浅白色款采用透明玻璃，通过底部卡榫和顶部球窝锁扣固定，拆卸无需工具。另一侧为密封钢板并内衬沥青材质以抑制噪音，同样采用卡扣结构。两侧板顶部均设有内凹式拉手，方便拆装。机箱侧面前部巧妙嵌入两条纵向铝制进气饰条，布满小圆孔，与浅白机箱形成鲜明视觉对比；内饰对应的防尘网可从前面板内侧抽出。虽然这种紧凑开孔理论上限流，但后续测试表明其散热表现尚可。机箱后部提供七个PCIe扩展槽，螺丝上方覆盖有装饰盖；电源位采用带防丢手拧螺丝的支架，便于安装；机箱左侧预置魔术贴用于理线。

机箱顶部更新为密集圆孔阵列，比Define 7的开孔更密集，但即使在顶部不装风扇时也能自然排热，且顶盖作为出风区域未设防尘网以优化气流。顶盖通过后部球窝卡扣即可轻松取下，露出风扇或冷排安装位。前置I/O面板位于顶缘，配备一个USB 3.2 Gen 2x2 Type-C（20Gbps）、两个USB 3.1 Gen 1 Type-A（5Gbps）、一枚印有Fractal标志的电源键、一个3.5mm音频复合插孔及顶部纤细LED指示灯。前面板可两步轻松拆卸：先拆顶盖，再扳动内部两个杠杆，即可接触前部的三枚140mm Momentum 14风扇与防尘网。底部边框为凸起的灰色塑料框架，四角配有橡胶脚垫，为电源留出约一英寸进风空间；底部防尘网从左侧（玻璃侧）抽出，方便日常清洁，无需挪动机箱。

内部结构采用经典的双仓设计，电源与线材独立于下仓。最为亮眼的设计之一是集成式前部空气导流板，可引导最下方前风扇的气流直接吹向显卡，避免冷风被电源仓浪费，并聚焦于高热核心部件。导流板正上方设有一个可调节显卡支撑架，直接固定于主板托盘上，仅需两颗螺丝即可上下移动数英寸，适用不同尺寸的显卡。主板托盘拥有丰富的开孔与走线槽，最大开孔位于CPU插槽正后方，便于在不拆主板的情况下安装散热器背板；其他开孔兼顾理线与支持背插式主板（如华硕BTF、技嘉Stealth、微星Project Zero系列）。机箱右侧设有大型灰色理线橡胶穿线孔，其固定牢固不易脱落，避免了常见松脱烦恼。由于支持背插主板，理线空间非常充足，主板托盘与侧板间拥有37mm（1.46英寸）距离，可轻松收纳杂乱线材。机箱还配备可滑动调节的塑料理线夹、多处预装魔术贴，以及用于固定8pin EPS供电线的背部理线带，让走线整洁有序。

存储方面，机箱背面设两个2.5/3.5英寸硬盘架，支持两个3.5寸硬盘或四个2.5寸硬盘，另有两个2.5寸安装位位于底部前空气导流板下方，总计最多可安装六个2.5寸硬盘。散热兼容性上，机箱内部空间宽敞：顶部支持双120/140mm风扇或最大280mm冷排，与主板之间留有约60mm余量；前部可安装三枚120/140mm风扇，或最大360mm冷排，若保留空气导流板，冷排最长405mm、厚度30mm；拆除导流板后可容纳长达435mm、厚度可达65mm的厚排；后部支持单120mm风扇。CPU散热器限高171mm，显卡限长368mm（安装前置风扇时），若前置30mm厚冷排则为338mm。电源仓限长180mm。预装三枚140mm、采用LCP（液晶聚合物）叶片的Momentum 14风扇于前部。防尘网覆盖顶部、前面和底部。

该机箱支持Mini-ITX、Micro ATX、ATX及E-ATX主板，扩展槽7个，尺寸为500×482×235mm（高×长×宽），重约13公斤（具体未列出）。官方定价为154.99美元，四种配置同价，提供两年质保。整体而言，Define One凭借圆润线条、高级材质和扎实的内部设计，在150美元价位段提供了越级的质感，同时延续了Define系列易于拆装、降噪静音的传统。文章作者表示，后续将对这款机箱进行全面的散热与噪音测试，以评估其与竞品的对比表现及能否跻身最佳机箱榜单，但就目前预览来看，Define One在工业设计和人性化细节上堪称Define家族至今最出色的作品之一。

items.title: AI data center investment projected to hit $32 trillion by 2050 — infrastructure spending estimated to exceed capital requirements for railways, electrification, or the internet
items.description: These investments aren't massive one-time expenses — data center operators are expected to upgrade their expensive GPUs and related infrastructure every four to six years, as new semiconductor technologies arrive on the market.
items.content: Copy link Facebook X Whatsapp Reddit Pinterest Flipboard Email Share this article 5 Join the conversation Follow us Add us as a preferred source on Google Newsletter Subscribe to our newsletter PricewaterhouseCoopers LLP (PwC) estimates that spending on AI data centers could reach as much as $31.6 trillion in the next decade and a half, with optimistic outlooks suggesting that capital expenditure could potentially hit $50 trillion. Bloomberg reports that this amount exceeds the spending that railways, electrification, or the internet required when they were being set up for the first time. It also pointed out that investments in AI data center infrastructure aren’t a one-time expense that would last decades, unlike railroad networks, the power grid, or fiber optic cables — instead, data center operators are expected to purchase new GPUs and related infrastructure every four to six years.Go deeper with TH Premium: AI and data centers (Image credit: Microsoft)The data center cooling state of playThe custom AI ASIC state of play America’s AI chip rules keep changing — and the rest of the world is paying the priceGTC 2026: Ian Buck press Q&A transcript — VP of Hyperscale and HPC speaks out on shelving CPX and shipping LPU decode this yearDemand for data center CPUs has surged, and AI agents are responsibleGPU development is happening at breakneck pace, with Nvidia, AMD, and other manufacturers releasing new generations every two to three years. In fact, one Google architect said that a data center GPU service life is only about one to three years, which has got some experts concerned that GPU depreciation could be the next big crisis for hyperscalers. “Railways. Electrification. The internet. Each required enormous amounts of capital and defined an era,” the publication reiterated from the report. “The AI infrastructure cycle underway dwarfs all three. This one resets every four to six years — and shows no signs of ending.”Nvidia and other chip manufacturers would be some of the biggest winners in this spending spree, but other hardware industries would also benefit, like networking equipment and even the copper material needed for running power inside data centers. PwC is confident in its forecast, especially as it claimed that both capital and demand for the AI build-out exist. It also broke down the investment in each region — spending in the U.S. is projected to hit $15.1 trillion, followed by the Asia-Pacific region, including China and India, at $8.2 trillion. Europe will likely spend $5.6 trillion, and it’s trailed by the Middle East at $1.1 trillion and Africa, with $255 billion.Latest Videos FromTom's HardwareWatch full video here: The AI build-out is not without risks, though. The report cited power availability, data sovereignty requirements, and chip availability as factors affecting the build-out. For example, data centers in the U.S. are forecasted to consume 20% of its total power supply by 2035, which is why operators are turning to natural gas turbines for on-site power. However, this has also led to jet engine shortages, which is why SpaceX has started in-house turbine blade manufacturing to cut delivery delays by up to 18 months. It also said the geopolitical tensions, like trade bans on rare earth elements and high-end chips, could cut the global investment forecast by 20%.There are still some concerns that the current AI boom is a bubble that will pop sooner or later. This is especially true as some AI tech companies currently have “hidden debt” worth around $1.65 trillion, while costs have started spiking as AI companies like OpenAI look for a path towards profitability. Despite that, Nvidia is still going full steam ahead, partnering with several firms to build a $500 billion AI infrastructure fund for further AI investments. items.titleZh: AI data center investment projected to hit $32 trillion by 2050 — infrastructure spending estimated to exceed capital requirements for railways, electrification, or the internet
items.descriptionZh:
普华永道（PwC）最新报告预测，未来十五年内全球AI数据中心的资本支出总额可能高达31.6万亿美元，在乐观情境下甚至有望触及50万亿美元。这一数字远超铁路、电气化或互联网等历史性基础设施建设初期的投入规模。报告特别指出，与传统基础设施不同，AI数据中心的投资并非一次性、可持续数十年的长期资产——铁路网络、电网或光纤光缆建成后可服役半个世纪，而AI数据中心的GPU和相关基础设施预计每四到六年就需要更换一轮。这意味着AI基建周期具有“自我重置”特性，持续不断产生新的巨额投资需求。

GPU更新换代的节奏惊人，Nvidia、AMD等厂商几乎每两到三年就推出新一代产品。谷歌一位架构师甚至表示，数据中心GPU的实际使用寿命仅约一至三年。这种快速迭代引发部分专家担忧：GPU折旧可能成为超大规模云厂商面临的下一场重大财务危机。报告援引原文强调：“铁路、电气化、互联网……每一项都需要巨额资本并定义一个时代。而当前的AI基础设施周期规模远超这三者之和，且每四到六年重置一次——并且看不到结束的迹象。”

在这场投资盛宴中，Nvidia等芯片制造商显然是最大赢家，但网络设备、数据中心内部供电所需的铜材料等相关硬件行业也将同步受益。普华永道对预测颇有信心，认为AI建设所需资本和市场需求均真实存在。报告还细分了各地区的投资规模：美国预计投入15.1万亿美元，居全球之首；包括中国和印度在内的亚太地区预计投入8.2万亿美元；欧洲为5.6万亿美元；中东为1.1万亿美元；非洲则为2550亿美元。

不过，AI建设并非没有风险。报告列举了电力供应不足、数据主权法规以及芯片可获取性等制约因素。例如，到2035年美国数据中心预计将消耗全国总供电量的20%，这迫使运营商转向燃气轮机实现现场发电。但此举又引发了燃气轮机（喷气发动机）短缺，SpaceX甚至为此自行生产涡轮叶片，以缩短长达18个月的交付延迟。此外，地缘政治紧张局势——如稀土元素和高端芯片的贸易禁令——可能导致全球AI投资预测削减20%。

目前市场仍存在对AI热潮是否为泡沫的担忧。部分AI科技公司的“隐性债务”规模已高达约1.65万亿美元，同时随着OpenAI等企业努力寻求盈利路径，成本也大幅飙升。尽管如此，Nvidia依然全力推进布局，正与多家公司合作建立规模达5000亿美元的AI基础设施投资基金，以支撑下一阶段的AI扩张。

items.title: Startups want to rent your idle gaming PC for AI tasks — Startups pitch an 'Airbnb for AI inference,' but profitability remains unproven
items.description: If your gaming rig spends most of its life doing nothing, a pair of startups would be willing to pay you something close to minimum wage for its downtime
items.content: Copy link Facebook X Whatsapp Reddit Pinterest Flipboard Email Share this article 5 Join the conversation Follow us Add us as a preferred source on Google Newsletter Subscribe to our newsletter If, like mine, your gaming rig spends most of its life doing nothing these days, a pair of startups would be willing to pay you something close to minimum wage for its downtime. Abu Dhabi-based Far Labs and Austin-based Evolving Edge are building marketplaces to farm AI inference out to idle consumer hardware, according to an IEEE Spectrum report.Far Labs plans to launch its Far AI platform in the coming weeks, claiming latency of 100 ms or less, while Evolving Edge is running an open beta. "Imagine Uber or Airbnb, but for AI inference computing tasks," Ilman Shazhaev, founder and CEO of Far Labs, told the outlet. Both companies are targeting smaller open-source models rather than frontier-scale workloads, and they’re joining established players, including the Utah-based Salad platform, which lists more than 60,000 daily active consumer GPUs on its network.Far Labs’ proprietary scheduler splits a model into pieces spread across multiple machines, and an orchestrator and a load balancer then reassemble the partial outputs into a response. Evolving Edge distributes jobs with Ray, the open-source framework used inside conventional data centers.Latest Videos FromTom's HardwareWatch full video here: Letting a stranger’s workload onto a personal machine obviously comes with some risks for hosts, such as malicious code ending up on the device or the person on the other end gaining access to local files. The two firms’ solution to this is isolation, with inference running as a sandboxed workload with encrypted communication and hard limits on GPU, CPU, memory, storage, and network access. Customers get no direct access to the host machine, and Evolving Edge has open-sourced its node software so hosts can audit what runs on their hardware.Salad sells consumer-GPU compute to customers for prices starting at $0.02 per hour, and the card’s owner only sees a slice of that… pie after the platform takes its cut. We examined Salad in 2021, back when its network mined Ethereum, estimating that the company had generated roughly $3.6 million from users' PCs while distributing $500,000 in rewards, which works out to about 14 cents on the dollar for the people supplying the silicon. You may like Meta reportedly plans to rent out its AI compute, sending AI stocks tumbling AI cryptomining network's 320,000 RTX 3090-class GPUs allegedly burn 112 megawatts of power on ‘zero useful AI computation’ Ditching the cloud for local AI — how I use two mini PCs to process millions of tokens a day and save money on costly API fees Electricity costs then chew through whatever's left. An RTX 4090 draws 350W to 450W under sustained load, roughly $40 to $50 a month at $0.15 per kWh if the card runs around the clock, so a rig earning less than that is effectively paying for the privilege of having a job. However, IEEE Spectrum's report doesn't include payout rates for either new platform.Both founders make the point that distributed networks ride out failures that otherwise cripple centralized clouds. John Federico, founder and CEO of Evolving Edge, cited the AWS outage last October that left Internet-connected smart beds stuck in their upright positions, and told IEEE Spectrum his network could lose 100 of 250,000 nodes “and it wouldn’t matter.”Stay On the Cutting Edge: Get the Tom's Hardware NewsletterGet Tom's Hardware's best news and in-depth reviews, straight to your inbox.Contact me with news and offers from other Future brandsReceive email from us on behalf of our trusted partners or sponsorsAll that aside, distributed AI compute has a credibility problem to overcome. A research preprint from June claimed that Pearl, a blockchain marketed as converting cryptocurrency mining into AI work, ran the equivalent of 320,000 RTX 3090-class GPUs on random matrix math while producing no useful AI computation. Far Labs and Evolving Edge route real customer inference jobs rather than token rewards, which puts them a step ahead of that model, but their cost and latency figures are unsubstantiated claims until, and if, the networks operate at scale. items.titleZh: 初创公司想租用你闲置的游戏电脑来执行AI任务 —— 初创公司推介‘AI推理的Airbnb’，但盈利能力仍未得到证实
items.descriptionZh:
如今许多游戏电脑大部分时间都处于闲置状态，两家初创公司正尝试让这些闲置的消费级硬件“打零工”，赚取接近最低工资的报酬。来自阿布扎比的Far Labs和奥斯汀的Evolving Edge正分别搭建平台，将AI推理任务分发到闲置的个人硬件上运行。Far Labs创始人兼CEO Ilman Shazhaev将这一模式比喻为“AI推理计算领域的Uber或Airbnb”。Far AI平台预计将在未来几周内上线，宣称推理延迟不超过100毫秒；Evolving Edge则已进入开放测试阶段。两家公司的目标并非前沿超大规模模型，而是更小型的开源模型，该赛道已有其他玩家，例如总部位于犹他州的Salad平台，其网络每天拥有超过6万块活跃消费级GPU。

技术层面，Far Labs采用专有调度器将模型分割成多个部分、分布在多台机器上执行，再由编排器和负载均衡器将部分输出组装为最终响应。Evolving Edge则使用了数据中心中常见的Ray开源框架来分发任务。把陌生人的工作负载放到个人设备上自然存在安全风险，比如恶意代码入侵或对方趁机访问本地文件。两家公司的应对方案是隔离：推理任务以沙箱化工作负载运行，配合加密通信以及对GPU、CPU、内存、存储和网络访问的严格限制。客户无法直接接触宿主机，Evolving Edge还将节点软件开源，以便主机方审计其设备上运行的内容。

经济账方面，Salad以每小时0.02美元起的价格向客户出售消费级GPU算力，而设备所有者只能在平台抽成后拿到一小部分。2021年Tom's Hardware曾考察过当时靠挖以太坊运转的Salad网络，估算该公司从用户电脑中赚取约360万美元，而分发给用户的奖励仅50万美元，相当于每支付给用户1美元，平台留下约86美分。此外，电费还会进一步侵蚀收益。以RTX 4090为例，持续负载时功耗在350瓦到450瓦之间，若全天候运行，按每千瓦时0.15美元计算，每月电费约为40至50美元。如果硬件挣的钱低于这个数额，实际是倒贴钱“上班”。IEEE Spectrum的报道并未披露两家新平台的分成比例。

两位创始人都强调，分布式网络具备更强的容错能力，能够扛住会瘫痪集中式云服务的故障。Evolving Edge创始人兼CEO John Federico提到，去年10月AWS宕机曾导致联网智能床卡在直立姿势无法放下，并称他的网络即使250,000个节点中损失100个也无关紧要。

尽管设想美好，分布式AI计算仍需克服信誉问题。今年6月一份研究预印本指出，一个名为Pearl的区块链项目标榜把加密货币挖矿转化为AI工作，实际上却让相当于32万张RTX 3090级别的GPU在跑随机矩阵计算，没有产生任何有用的AI计算。Far Labs和Evolving Edge传输的是真实客户的推理作业，而非代币奖励，在这方面比Pearl的模式更进一步，但其成本和延迟数据目前只是未经证实的主张，需要等网络大规模运行后才能得到验证。

items.title: China's EUV technology 'at a similar stage to ASML in 2004,' analyst claims — Beijing's semiconductor industry remains well behind Western rivals
items.description: Despite rumors, there is no evidence that Chinese makers of lithography tools can produce immersion lithography scanners in quantity.
items.content: Copy link Facebook X Whatsapp Reddit Pinterest Flipboard Email Share this article 0 Join the conversation Follow us Add us as a preferred source on Google Newsletter Subscribe to our newsletter China's ability to produce lithography tools is comparable to that of market leader ASML sometime in 2004, an analyst with UBS wrote in a note to clients. The situation may change in the next two or five years when Chinese companies start producing immersion DUV lithography systems in mass quantities, and Chinese chipmakers begin to deploy them for production of actual chips. However, China's semiconductor industry will remain well behind Western industry. "They seem to be at a similar stage to ASML in 2004," wrote Francois-Xavier Bouvignies, an analyst with UBS, in a note for clients, reports Bloomberg.Go deeper with TH Premium: Chipmaking (Image credit: tsmc)Analyzing TSMC's fab expansion roadmap — multi-fab N2 ramp, CoWoS, SoIC, and uncorking bottlenecksLeading-edge foundry roadmaps for TSMC, Intel, and SamsungASML's roadmap for chipmaking lithography tools examinedChinese chipmaking tool roadmaps examinedFor years, China's pursuit of semiconductor self-sufficiency stemmed from its ability to produce mainstream chips on trailing nodes using fairly advanced, though not the latest, tools from leading producers such as ASML, KLA, and Lam Research. In recent years, China found itself in a new reality in which it could no longer obtain the latest chipmaking tools and had to build them domestically. Although companies like ACM Research, AMEC, and Naura have developed world-class chemical wafer deposition, cleaning, etching, and oxidation/diffusion tools that are now mass-produced and used by Chinese chipmakers, none of the Chinese companies have managed to develop a competitive lithography machine that can be used to make chips on more or less modern nodes and initiate its mass production.Photolithography is generally considered the most technologically complex and demanding individual process in advanced semiconductor manufacturing. Firstly, lithography systems themselves are extraordinarily complex and contain tens of thousands of individual components. Secondly, the required positional accuracy is extraordinary, as a modern lithography scanner needs excellent resolution, overlay, focus control, scanner-to-scanner matching, CD uniformity, and line edge roughness, just to name some of the requirements. Finally, a competitive litho system must guarantee predictable uptime, defect density, and performance. Perhaps the key thing here is that all of the required features must be achieved without compromises, as, for example, a machine with high resolution and ideal uniformity that can process one wafer per hour cannot be used for mass production.Latest Videos FromTom's HardwareWatch full video here: Historically, over a dozen companies produced lithography tools. However, as they became more complex, only ASML, Canon, and Nikon survived, with ASML being the undisputed market leader and the only maker of EUV lithography scanners.As China is essentially developing a parallel semiconductor ecosystem, there have been reports of multiple entities working on lithography systems, including Shanghai Micro Electronics Equipment (SMEE), AMIES (which seems to be a SMEE spin-off that includes Aishengna and Yuliangsheng units), SiCarrier (reportedly controlled by Huawei), and even Naura (which denies that it is developing litho tools). SMEE, which was established in 2002, is by far the most important established Chinese manufacturer of litho tools. Meanwhile, so far none of China-based makers of lithography have established mass production of immersion DUV scanners capable of producing chips at 45nm and below. You may like Shanghai Aishengna named as the maker of China's first domestic immersion DUV chipmaking tools Chinese chipmaking tool roadmaps examined — Beijing's nascent lithography tools target DUV production at five machines a year, and an EUV prototype with no chips China begins mass production of homegrown immersion chipmaking machines in major breakthrough, report claims SMEE reportedly formally introduced its first immersion DUV lithography system called SSA/800-10W and capable of making chips on nodes down to 28nm back in 2023. However, there have been no evidence that SMEE has indeed started mass production of the SSA/800-10W and that it has been adopted by a single manufacturer for mass production of chips. While it is conceivable that not all chipmakers announce deployment of breakthrough tools, especially keeping in mind that Chinese vendors like SMEE have plenty of foreign suppliers, we would have seen at least some indirect evidence (starting from procurement/acceptance records as well as component orders all the way to job postings and scientific papers) that SMEE started shipments of the SSA/800-10W in 2023 – 2024 by now, assuming of course that there were any shipments.Interestingly, but the reports about China-made immersion DUV scanners now mass-produced by Shanghai Aishengna Electronic Technology Group (a unit, or an affiliate of SMEE) re-emerged this July, again, without any evidence. This time around, the reports did not even mention targeted nodes or throughput capabilities. To make matters even more suspicious is the lack of reports about shipments of evaluation tools to chipmakers (like ASML does this with its High-NA EUV machines) as well as preliminary results of their process qualifications (like Intel does with ASML's High-NA EUV machines). Stay On the Cutting Edge: Get the Tom's Hardware Newsletter Get Tom's Hardware's best news and in-depth reviews, straight to your inbox. Contact me with news and offers from other Future brands Receive email from us on behalf of our trusted partners or sponsors For a first-ever Chinese immersion scanner, it is reasonable to expect Chinese chipmakers to use it on engineering wafers, characterize it against ASML machines, develop recipes, identify drawbacks, and pass that information back to SMEE, something that should take about a year. Only once that first machine performs adequately does it make sense to order and qualify multiple SSA/800-10W units for mass production. In fact, such qualification will likely take another year for a single layer and more time for additional layers. To that end, an insertion of an all-new lithography scanner into an existing flow will take at least two years, but likely more. To that end, once SMEE (or its business units) and its customers figure out how the first Chinese immersion scanner should work, these scanners will still be far from mass deployment.In any case, without any real indicators that Chinese makers of wafer fab tools can produce and ship immersion lithography scanners to customers, we can only state what the UBS analyst did: China's lithography industry is in a position where ASML was in the mid-2000s. items.titleZh: China's EUV technology 'at a similar stage to ASML in 2004,' analyst claims — Beijing's semiconductor industry remains well behind Western rivals
items.descriptionZh:
据彭博社报道，瑞银(UBS)分析师Francois-Xavier Bouvignies在致客户的报告中指出，中国当前制造光刻设备的能力大致相当于市场领导者ASML在2004年时的水平。预计未来两到五年内，中国公司可能开始量产浸没式DUV光刻系统，中国芯片制造商也可能将其用于真实芯片的生产。不过，即便实现这一点，中国半导体产业仍会明显落后于西方先进国家。

过去很长一段时间，中国追求半导体自给自足的主要途径，是利用ASML、科磊（KLA）、泛林（Lam Research）等全球龙头提供的“较先进但并非最新一代”的设备来制造成熟制程芯片。随着出口管制收紧，中国已经无法获得最尖端的芯片制造工具，只能转向自主研发。目前，盛美（ACM Research）、中微公司（AMEC）、北方华创（Naura）等中国企业已在化学沉积、清洗、刻蚀和氧化/扩散等半导体设备领域拿出世界级产品，并已在量产线上大量使用。然而在光刻机这一公认最复杂、最尖端的领域，目前还没有任何一家中国企业成功研发出能够用于相对现代制程、并通过严格量产验证的高竞争力光刻设备。

光刻是先进半导体制造中最难逾越的技术环节。现代光刻扫描仪由数万个精密零部件组成，需要同时具备极高的分辨率、极佳的套刻精度、焦深控制、机台间匹配、关键尺寸均匀性和线边缘粗糙度表现；更重要的是，光刻设备还必须保证足够的量产吞吐能力和可预测的稳定运行时间、低缺陷密度，不能为了追求某一项参数而牺牲产能——例如一台每小时只能处理一片晶圆的高精度光刻机是没有量产价值的。正因技术挑战巨大，历史上十余家光刻设备厂商如今只剩下ASML、佳能和尼康，其中EUV光刻机更是由ASML独家垄断。

为了打造一套不依赖西方供应、平行的半导体生态系统，中国已有多个团队在推进光刻机研发，包括上海微电子装备（SMEE）、据称是从SMEE分拆并吸收Aishengna和Yuliangsheng业务的AMIES、传闻由华为控制的SiCarrier，以及否认涉足光刻的北方华创。SMEE成立于2002年，是目前中国最重要的老牌光刻设备企业，但迄今没有能量产可用于45nm及以下制程芯片的浸没式DUV扫描仪。SMEE曾在2023年正式发布首台国产浸没式DUV光刻系统SSA/800-10W，号称能够制造28nm及以下节点芯片，但外界始终没有看到该设备真正进入量产、被任何晶圆厂采用并用于大规模芯片生产的证据。如果SMEE已经在2023至2024年间发货，通常会出现一些间接迹象，例如采购与验收记录、关键零部件订单、相关招聘、论文或专利，但这些都未出现。

2024年7月前后，关于上海Aishengna（SMEE的关联公司或业务部门）已经“量产国产浸没式DUV光刻机”的消息再次兴起，但同样缺乏可靠证据。报道不仅没有提供目标工艺节点，也没有给出设备的吞吐性能数据，更像是一次期待而非事实。对于中国第一台真正浸没式扫描仪而言，合理的推进节奏应当是：芯片厂先把它用于工程晶圆做工艺开发，与ASML同类机台进行比对，建立配方，找出短板并反馈给设备商。这个过程大约需要一年；只有在第一台设备达标后，企业才会订购多台设备，并针对不同工艺层进行后续认证，单层工艺验证可能还要再花一年以上时间。也就是说，一台全新的光刻扫描仪进入成熟量产线至少需要两年，更多时候会更久，因此即便SMEE及其客户已经掌握方向，距离大规模部署依然很遥远。

items.titleZh: Acer's Swift Blade 14 weighs just 1.76 pounds and uses Wildcat Lake — company introduces new sub-brand ahead of IFA tradeshow
items.descriptionZh:
宏碁（Acer）在推出平价定位的 Swift Air 14 之后，又基于英特尔的 Wildcat Lake 平台发布了多款轻薄机型，以完善其中端产品线。在 IFA 大展前夕，宏碁推出了全新子品牌 Swift Blade 14，主打仅 799 克（1.76 磅）的极致便携重量，同时还有一款 16 英寸的 Swift Air 16。

Swift Blade 14 是 Swift 系列新增的轻量级产品线。为了实现极轻的机身，其外壳采用了铝镁合金与碳纤维的混合材料，既保证了结构强度，又把重量压到了不足 800 克。整机最薄处约 0.51 英寸（约 13 毫米），放在背包中几乎没有存在感。该机提供棉花糖白和棉花糖蓝两种配色。硬件上，它搭载基于英特尔 Wildcat Lake 架构的处理器，可选型号从 Core 3 304 一直延伸到 Core 7 350，配合 12GB LPDDR5 板载内存和集成 Intel Graphics 显卡，最高可选 1TB PCIe Gen 4 NVMe SSD。接口方面，提供了三个 USB 3.2 Gen 1 Type-C 端口（其中一个是纯数据口）以及一个耳机插孔。屏幕为 14 英寸，可选 2880 × 1800 分辨率、400 尼特亮度、90Hz 刷新率 OLED 面板，也有更平民化的 1920 × 1200 OLED 或 IPS LCD 选项。其他配置还包括 50Wh 电池、Wi-Fi 6、蓝牙 5.3 和 1080p 摄像头。

16 英寸的 Swift Air 16 则可以理解为 Computex 上 Swift Air 14 的放大升级版，不过在体验上更进一步。它保留了铝合金机身、Thunderbolt 4 接口和 100W 电源适配器等特性，并加入了 OLED 屏幕和四扬声器系统。外观提供元素蓝、鼠尾草绿和砂岩金三种颜色，不过不同市场配色会有差异。配置上，处理器同样最高可选 Core 7 350，内存最高可扩展到 16GB LPDDR5x，存储则最高为 512GB PCIe Gen 4 SSD。该机的屏幕选择更丰富，最高配为 16 英寸 2880 × 1800 OLED，具有 600 尼特亮度和 120Hz 刷新率；另外还有 1920 × 1200 OLED 或支持触控的 IPS LCD 可选。它配备 70Wh 大电池，并升级到 Wi-Fi 6E（AX211）和蓝牙 5.3，摄像头也加入了红外人脸识别功能。

从技术原理来看，Wildcat Lake 是英特尔面向轻薄低功耗设备推出的新一代处理器平台，核心特点是将 CPU、GPU 和内存控制器高度集成，搭配 LPDDR5/LPDDR5x 低功耗内存可以有效降低主板占用面积，帮助厂商把机身做薄做轻。此次宏碁给出了从 Core 3 304 到 Core 7 350 不同档位的选择，显示出该平台覆盖多级性能市场的弹性。Swift Blade 14 的轻量化关键，除了依赖这种低功耗芯片的散热压力较小之外，混合金属与碳纤维的材料工艺也功不可没。

对比来看，Swift Blade 14 更强调“随身便携”，在存储上限（最高 1TB）和重量控制上更突出，但电池容量和无线规格相对保守；Swift Air 16 则更倾向影音娱乐和全场景连接，凭借 70Wh 电池、120Hz 高亮 OLED 屏幕、Thunderbolt 4 和 Wi-Fi 6E，适合需要长时间在户外使用大屏笔记本办公或追剧的用户。

两款产品都计划在 2027 年第一季度于北美市场发售，而欧洲、中东及非洲地区会率先在 12 月发货。随着 IFA 开幕，宏碁预计还会披露价格与更多销售细节。

The company claims the new model “works harder” than Gemini 3.7 Flash by performing more reasoning steps on complex tasks and “calling tools iteratively.” It has the same introductory pricing as 3.7 Flash, $0.75 per million input tokens and $3.75 per million output tokens, but could still end up costing users more. Google warns that “the model might use more tokens to maximize performance, especially at higher effort levels.” Developers can keep using Gemini 3.7 Flash if they want to minimize token usage.Gemini 3.8 Flash’s launch was followed by some early impressions online. Artificial Analysis highlighted the model’s pricing, saying Gemini 3.8 Flash is “the cheapest we’ve measured at this level of intelligence. This is up ~40% from Gemini 3.7 Flash despite unchanged per-token pricing, driven by a 30% increase in output tokens per task and more turns on agentic evaluations.”Aigora.ai CEO John Ennis compared Gemini 3.8 Flash to Anthropic’s models, saying it offers “Opus 5 coding quality but at a fraction of the cost and super fast,” adding, “This is going to be so awesome for things like making remotion videos.”Google says Gemini 3.8 Flash offers “significant improvements” for software engineering and autonomous AI agents. It outperforms its predecessor and other frontier models on the DeepSWE v1.1 software engineering benchmark, including Anthropic’s Fable 5, which got an upgrade earlier this week that also promises stronger performance at a lower price, by cutting the price to use cached data.Google’s new model also outperformed its competitors on the Vals Finance Agent V2 benchmark and Harvey’s Legal Agent benchmark. However, the new model also “ships with safeguards against misuse in the domains of Chemical, Biological, Radiological, and Nuclear (CBRN) and cyber offense.”Google also released Gemini 3.8 Flash Cyber alongside its new Fairwind Program, which is limited to governments and “trusted partners.” The program, whose 650 members include CrowdStrike and the Center for Internet Security, offers access to 3.8 Flash Cyber and Google’s CodeMender agent, which Google says can help “autonomously find and fix vulnerabilities, protecting critical infrastructure, public services, and national security.” Gemini 3.8 Flash is available now for consumers with a Google AI Pro or Ultra subscription, as well as developers and enterprise users.

history.titleZh: 谷歌称其新的Gemini 3.8 Flash模型“工作更努力”，但成本可能更高
history.descriptionZh:
Google 在 Gemini 3.7 Flash 发布仅数周后便推出了新一代 Gemini 3.8 Flash。官方宣称，新模型在复杂任务中会执行更多推理步骤，并能够“迭代式地调用工具”，因此比前代“更努力地工作”。在定价上，Gemini 3.8 Flash 的入门价格与 3.7 Flash 保持一致：输入每百万 token 0.75 美元、输出每百万 token 3.75 美元，但由于新模型可能通过消耗更多 token 来追求更高性能，尤其是在高努力级别下，用户的实际成本可能上升。Google 也提示，希望严格控制 token 用量的开发者仍可继续使用 Gemini 3.7 Flash。

早期评测和用户反馈进一步揭示了其成本特性。Artificial Analysis 指出，Gemini 3.8 Flash 在同等智能水平下是“我们测过的最便宜的模型”，但单任务总成本依然比 3.7 Flash 高出约 40%，主要原因包括每个任务的输出 token 数量增加了 30%，以及在智能体评估中的交互轮次更多。Aigora.ai CEO John Ennis 将它与 Anthropic 的模型对比，认为其在编码任务上达到了“Opus 5 的质量”，但成本和速度优势明显，并特别提到它非常适合用于制作 remotion 视频等场景。

在技术性能方面，Google 表示 Gemini 3.8 Flash 在软件工程和自主 AI 智能体能力上实现了“显著提升”。它在 DeepSWE v1.1 软件工程基准测试中超越了前代及其他前沿模型，包括 Anthropic 本周早些时候刚刚升级的 Fable 5——该模型同样希望通过下调缓存数据的使用价格来提供更强劲且更经济的性能。此外，Gemini 3.8 Flash 还在 Vals Finance Agent V2 金融智能体基准和 Harvey 法律智能体基准上领先竞争对手。

为了防范滥用，新模型加入了针对化学、生物、放射性、核（CBRN）以及网络攻击等领域的保护措施。Google 还同步发布了面向政府和“受信伙伴”的 Gemini 3.8 Flash Cyber，以及名为 Fairwind 的专项计划。该计划目前拥有 650 个成员，包括 CrowdStrike 和互联网安全中心，参与者可以访问 Gemini 3.8 Flash Cyber 和 Google 的 CodeMender 智能体。后者能够“自主发现并修复漏洞，保护关键基础设施、公共服务和国家安全”。目前，Gemini 3.8 Flash 已面向 Google AI Pro/Ultra 订阅消费者、开发者及企业用户开放。

history.title: Microsoft will expand Windows 11 Memory Integrity feature to more PCs starting in October — security feature reduces gaming performance on some systems
history.description: Microsoft will begin enabling Memory Integrity by default on more eligible Windows PCs through quality updates in October, expanding kernel-level protection while preserving existing opt-outs for users who previously disabled the feature.
history.content: Copy link Facebook X Whatsapp Reddit Pinterest Flipboard Email Share this article 3 Join the conversation Follow us Add us as a preferred source on Google Newsletter Subscribe to our newsletter Microsoft will begin automatically enabling its Memory Integrity security feature on a broader range of eligible Windows PCs through quality updates starting in October 2026, extending the kernel-level protection to more existing devices by default. In a September 1 blog post, Microsoft said the rollout will provide stronger protection for more devices against attacks targeting the Windows kernel, while PCs that already have Memory Integrity deliberately disabled will retain their existing configuration.“Windows quality updates will begin enabling memory integrity protection on eligible devices,” Microsoft said. The updates will also enable Virtualization-based Security (VBS) where required, which provides the isolated environment underlying Memory Integrity. Before making the change, Windows will automatically assess each device using what Microsoft describes as readiness signals covering its hardware capabilities, compatibility, and performance.The October rollout is basically an expansion of Microsoft’s existing default-enablement policy. Memory Integrity is already switched on by default on clean Windows 11 installations that meet Microsoft’s hardware requirements, as well as on Secured-core PCs. Current requirements include an 8th Gen or newer Intel processor for Windows 11 22H2, an AMD Zen 2 or newer processor, at least 8GB of RAM on x64 systems, an SSD of at least 64GB, compatible drivers, and enabled hardware virtualization. Automatic activation under that policy applies to clean installations and not upgrades of existing devices.Latest Videos FromTom's HardwareWatch full video here: Memory Integrity — also known as Hypervisor-Protected Code Integrity (HVCI) — has existed since the Windows 10 era and was originally released as part of Microsoft’s Device Guard security technology. It uses VBS and the Windows hypervisor to move kernel-mode code-integrity checks into an isolated environment, helping prevent malicious or untrusted code and drivers from executing in the Windows kernel. Windows 10 generally left the protection optional outside configurations such as S mode, while Windows 11 made it more of a default security feature on compatible new installations.The feature comes with a performance wrinkle familiar to PC gamers, leading many gamers to disable it. Microsoft acknowledged in 2022 that Memory Integrity and Virtual Machine Platform could affect gaming performance on some Windows 11 configurations, and advised gamers prioritizing performance that they could temporarily disable these protections while playing, warning that doing so reduces security. The company’s own gaming guidance subsequently continued to recommend temporarily disabling Memory Integrity and VMP where they interfere with gaming performance. You may like Microsoft vows to make Windows 11 fly on 8GB RAM amid memory shortage Microsoft extends free Windows 10 security updates for a second year AMD will reinstate memory encryption on Ryzen 9000 CPUs through a BIOS update in July — TSME is coming back after 'valuable community feedback' The security feature’s impact on performance depends on the hardware. Microsoft says Memory Integrity performs better on newer processors with hardware features designed to accelerate the required isolation, while older CPUs relying on software emulation can experience a larger performance hit. Driver compatibility can also prevent activation, with Microsoft documenting issues ranging from malfunctioning software to incompatible gaming anti-cheat solutions.For most users, the October change requires no action. Eligible PCs will be evaluated and updated automatically, while administrator policies and previous user choices remain in place. Microsoft specifically says systems where Memory Integrity has already been disabled “won’t be automatically changed by this rollout,” leaving gamers and other users who previously opted out in control of the setting.Stay On the Cutting Edge: Get the Tom's Hardware NewsletterGet Tom's Hardware's best news and in-depth reviews, straight to your inbox.Contact me with news and offers from other Future brandsReceive email from us on behalf of our trusted partners or sponsors Follow Tom's Hardware on Google News, or add us as a preferred source, to get our latest news, analysis, & reviews in your feeds.

history.titleZh: 微软将自10月起将Windows 11的内存完整性功能扩展到更多PC——该安全功能会降低某些系统的游戏性能
history.descriptionZh:
微软昨日通过官方博客宣布了一项重要的安全更新计划：自2026年10月起，将通过Windows质量更新（Quality Updates）在更广泛的符合条件的PC上自动启用“内存完整性”（Memory Integrity）功能。这意味着这项针对Windows内核的防护措施，将从目前主要覆盖新装机的方式，扩展为面向更多存量设备默认开启。微软在9月1日的博文中明确表示，Windows质量更新将开始为符合条件的设备启用内存完整性保护，同时也会在需要的地方启用作为其底层支撑的基于虚拟化的安全（VBS）功能。在执行变更之前，Windows会根据硬件能力、兼容性和性能等多维度的“就绪信号”对每台设备进行自动评估。

此次2026年10月的推广，实质上是对微软现有默认启用策略的延伸。目前，在符合微软硬件要求的干净Windows 11安装以及安全核心PC（Secured-core PCs）上，内存完整性已被默认开启。以Windows 11 22H2为例，现有要求包括：第八代或更新的Intel处理器、AMD Zen 2或更新的处理器、x64系统至少8GB内存、至少64GB的SSD、兼容的驱动程序以及已启用的硬件虚拟化。值得注意的是，此前该策略下的自动激活仅适用于全新安装，而非对现有设备的升级，而到2026年10月后的这项新举措将使升级的已有设备也纳入默认启用的范围，但已有用户手动选择关闭的机器除外。

内存完整性，又被称为虚拟机监控程序保护的代码完整性（HVCI），最早可追溯至Windows 10时代，它最初作为微软Device Guard安全技术的一部分发布。其核心原理是利用VBS和Windows虚拟机监控程序（Hypervisor），将内核模式的代码完整性检查移入一个与操作系统隔离的安全环境中运行，从而有效阻止恶意或不受信任的代码与驱动程序在Windows内核中执行，从根本上保护系统核心免受攻击。在Windows 10时代，除了S模式等特定配置外，该保护普遍是可选项；而Windows 11则在兼容的新安装中将其定位为默认安全功能。

这项安全特性带来的性能损耗始终是PC玩家圈热议的话题，也是不少游戏玩家选择关闭它的原因。微软曾在2022年承认，内存完整性和虚拟机平台（Virtual Machine Platform）可能会对某些Windows 11配置下的游戏性能造成影响，并建议以性能为优先的用户可以在游戏时暂时关闭这些保护，但同时警告这会降低系统安全性。微软自家的游戏优化指南甚至也持续建议，在内存完整性和VMP干扰游戏性能时暂时将其禁用。需要指出的是，该功能对性能的实际影响高度依赖于硬件配置——微软称，在配备专门硬件加速隔离能力的新款处理器上，内存完整性表现相对更好；而依赖软件模拟的较老CPU则可能面临更明显的性能折损。此外，驱动程序兼容性也可能阻止该功能的启用，微软记录在案的问题既包括软件故障，也包括与某些游戏反作弊解决方案的不兼容。

对于大多数普通用户而言，2026年10月的这项变更无需任何手动操作：符合条件的PC将被自动评估并完成更新，而管理员策略和用户此前做出的选择也会得到尊重。微软特别强调，凡是已经手动关闭内存完整性的系统，都不会因这次推广而自动被重新打开。这意味着此前出于性能或其他原因选择关闭的玩家和用户，将保留对该设置的控制权，不会被强制变更。这项举措体现了微软在默认安全防护与用户自主选择之间寻求平衡的思路，未来几年，将推动更多存量Windows设备在无需用户干预的情况下具备抵御内核级攻击的底层能力。

history.title: GoPro to expand into AI data centers after $285 million merger with optical-photonics company — move to solve camera maker’s financial woes, move manufacturing back into the US
history.description: GoPro is merging with optical-photonics company Starman Optical in a deal worth at least $285 million. This move will wipe out the company's $92 million outstanding debt, let it start manufacturing its cameras in the U.S., and expand its portfolio to include optical transceivers for AI data centers.
history.content: Copy link Facebook X Whatsapp Reddit Pinterest Flipboard Email Share this article 0 Join the conversation Follow us Add us as a preferred source on Google Newsletter Subscribe to our newsletter GoPro just announced a merger with Starman Optical, Inc., an optical-photonics company, saying that the deal would allow the combined entity to produce U.S.-made optical transceivers for use in AI data centers. According to the press release, Starman will pay shareholders $285 million in cash for the action camera company, amounting to $1.14 per share, and will also pay off its outstanding debt of $92 million. Despite that, current GoPro investors will retain 10% ownership of the post-merger company.Go deeper with TH Premium: AI and data centers (Image credit: Microsoft)The data center cooling state of playThe custom AI ASIC state of play America’s AI chip rules keep changing — and the rest of the world is paying the priceGTC 2026: Ian Buck press Q&A transcript — VP of Hyperscale and HPC speaks out on shelving CPX and shipping LPU decode this yearDemand for data center CPUs has surged, and AI agents are responsibleStarman said that the move will give it access to GoPro’s intellectual property, which amounts to more than 2,500 patents, as well as its imaging solutions, advanced optics, and other technologies that it has developed. This deal is crucial in keeping the camera company afloat, especially as it has recently faced declining sales and increasing costs, leading the camera maker to warn investors that there is “substantial doubt about the company’s ability to continue.”On the other hand, the merger would expand GoPro’s portfolio to include optical transceivers, which are getting increased demand as AI data centers transition to fiber optics for their networking needs. Aside from data centers, the deal would also allow GoPro to expand into defense, government, robotics, and the aerospace industries, where it “intends to leverage its IP, optics, and imaging capabilities” to supply the increasing demand for solutions made within the U.S.Latest Videos FromTom's HardwareWatch full video here: While GoPro has successfully moved its manufacturing out of China to protect its supply chain from U.S. tariffs, it still has no local manufacturing. So, this merger would allow it to have production within American borders and help isolate it from further economic instability brought about by surprise tariff announcements.This could help it secure its future, especially as the FCC has recently been making moves to keep foreign-made tech like routers, LiDAR-equipped drones, and robots. It also makes sense for the two companies to partner — even though consumer action cameras and optical transceivers for data centers sound like they have nothing in common, they share a lot of technologies between them, like imaging sensors and advanced lenses or optics. Struggling shoemaker and apparel brand Allbirds pivoted towards it earlier this year, resulting in a 580% jump in its stock price after the announcement, although it has since settled back down to its pre-announcement prices. AI data centers are indeed a tempting investment, with consultancy firm PricewaterhouseCoopers saying that investment on the technology could hit $32 trillion by 2050.
